title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has made a formal decision regarding its approach to artificial intelligence governance. This decision outlines the office's stance and intended actions, providing guidance on how AI systems should be managed and regulated.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The policy document outlines the process for filling an open position in the AI Office, specifically targeting technology specialists who can advance AI research and development. It details the qualifications, responsibilities, and selection criteria to ensure the chosen specialist supports the organization’s AI initiatives and maintains high standards of technical competence.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The policy document announces an open position for a Lead Scientific Adviser within the AI Office, outlining the key responsibilities and expectations for the role. It highlights the need for a candidate with strong scientific expertise, strategic vision, and the ability to guide AI research and policy initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy explains how the organization fills vacancies for legal officer roles within its AI office. It sets out the required qualifications, responsibilities, and steps for hiring and appointment to ensure compliance and effective governance.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy establishes an AI office dedicated to developing and overseeing AI guidelines, and outlines the responsibilities and qualifications for policy officers. It also sets procedures for filling vacancies within the office, ensuring continuity in AI governance.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with reviewing the scientific and technical aspects of the European Union’s AI Act. They evaluate evidence, assess risks, and advise lawmakers on how to regulate AI safely and effectively.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document proposes a standardized approach to AI policy across the organization, detailing guidelines for development, deployment, and oversight. It aims to promote consistency, safety, and regulatory compliance in AI initiatives.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The CoP Consultation Notice announces a call for input on developing or updating a Community of Practice. It invites stakeholders to share ideas and help shape the policies and guidelines that will guide the community’s work.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document announces a call for people or organizations to express interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP). It provides details on how to submit expressions of interest and the criteria that will be used to select participants.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The policy describes the iterative drafting process used by the Community of Practice to develop and refine AI guidelines. It outlines how drafts are repeatedly written, reviewed, and improved until a final version is reached.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document shows a visual timeline that maps out the main stages and milestones of drafting the AI policy. It helps readers see the sequence and timing of decisions and actions taken during the policy’s creation.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document is a first draft of a Code of Practice, outlining recommended standards and guidelines for responsible AI use and development. It aims to set clear expectations and accountability measures to promote ethical, safe, and transparent AI practices.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document is the second draft of a Code of Practice, outlining standards and guidelines for responsible AI development and deployment. It provides clear principles and best practices to ensure the ethical, safe, and transparent use of artificial intelligence.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document lays out the third draft of a Code of Practice for the responsible development and use of AI, providing clear guidelines and standards that organizations should follow to ensure ethical, safe, and trustworthy AI systems. It covers key areas such as transparency, fairness, accountability, risk assessment, and ongoing monitoring to help companies comply with regulatory expectations and protect users.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposal to create a set of rules and guidelines for how artificial intelligence should be developed, used, and monitored. It seeks to promote safety, transparency, and cooperation among all parties so that AI can benefit society while minimizing potential risks.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final outlines a comprehensive set of principles and guidelines for the development, deployment, and governance of artificial intelligence, emphasizing transparency, fairness, accountability, and human oversight. It serves as a binding framework intended to promote responsible AI practices across sectors and stakeholders.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This document lists the specific types of AI behavior and applications that are prohibited. It serves as a guide for developers to avoid implementing or deploying AI systems that fall into these disallowed categories.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy explains how to identify and describe what counts as an AI system. It offers clear criteria and examples to help organizations classify and label their AI technologies accurately.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: The policy outlines how the organization plans to improve communication to support startups and foster innovation. It includes strategies for sharing resources, engaging stakeholders, and building networks to boost entrepreneurial growth.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start‑Ups is a program designed to help emerging technology companies access high‑performance computing resources across Europe. It offers startups free or discounted access to supercomputing facilities, training, and support to accelerate their research and product development.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar will cover key concepts and best practices for managing risks in various contexts, from business projects to technology deployments. It will provide actionable strategies for identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential threats to achieve safer and more reliable outcomes.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar provides an overview of risk management principles and how they apply to AI systems, covering identification, assessment, and mitigation of potential risks. It also discusses regulatory compliance, governance frameworks, and best practices for building resilient AI solutions.
